records.title: Privacy Policy
records.content:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: https://shogranvalley.com.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

records.title: Refund and Returns Policy
records.content:
This is a sample page.

Overview

Our refund and returns policy lasts 30 days. If 30 days have passed since your purchase, we can’t offer you a full refund or exchange.

To be eligible for a return, your item must be unused and in the same condition that you received it. It must also be in the original packaging.

Several types of goods are exempt from being returned. Perishable goods such as food, flowers, newspapers or magazines cannot be returned. We also do not accept products that are intimate or sanitary goods, hazardous materials, or flammable liquids or gases.

Additional non-returnable items:

  • Gift cards
  • Downloadable software products
  • Some health and personal care items

To complete your return, we require a receipt or proof of purchase.

Please do not send your purchase back to the manufacturer.

There are certain situations where only partial refunds are granted:

  • Book with obvious signs of use
  • CD, DVD, VHS tape, software, video game, cassette tape, or vinyl record that has been opened.
  • Any item not in its original condition, is damaged or missing parts for reasons not due to our error.
  • Any item that is returned more than 30 days after delivery

Refunds

Once your return is received and inspected, we will send you an email to notify you that we have received your returned item. We will also notify you of the approval or rejection of your refund.

If you are approved, then your refund will be processed, and a credit will automatically be applied to your credit card or original method of payment, within a certain amount of days.

Late or missing refunds

If you haven’t received a refund yet, first check your bank account again.

Then contact your credit card company, it may take some time before your refund is officially posted.

Next contact your bank. There is often some processing time before a refund is posted.

If you’ve done all of this and you still have not received your refund yet, please contact us at {email address}.

Sale items

Only regular priced items may be refunded. Sale items cannot be refunded.

Exchanges

We only replace items if they are defective or damaged. If you need to exchange it for the same item, send us an email at {email address} and send your item to: {physical address}.

Gifts

If the item was marked as a gift when purchased and shipped directly to you, you’ll receive a gift credit for the value of your return. Once the returned item is received, a gift certificate will be mailed to you.

If the item wasn’t marked as a gift when purchased, or the gift giver had the order shipped to themselves to give to you later, we will send a refund to the gift giver and they will find out about your return.

Shipping returns

To return your product, you should mail your product to: {physical address}.

You will be responsible for paying for your own shipping costs for returning your item. Shipping costs are non-refundable. If you receive a refund, the cost of return shipping will be deducted from your refund.

Depending on where you live, the time it may take for your exchanged product to reach you may vary.

If you are returning more expensive items, you may consider using a trackable shipping service or purchasing shipping insurance. We don’t guarantee that we will receive your returned item.

Need help?

Contact us at {email} for questions related to refunds and returns.

records.title: Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran Prices 2026 – Room Rates Per Night
records.content:
Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran prices start from Rs. 20,500 per night for a Standard Room and go up to Rs. 28,500 per night for the VIP/Executive category. If you are planning a Kaghan Valley trip in 2026 and want to know exactly what a night at Shogran’s most famous resort costs, this guide breaks down every room category, what is included in the rate, and how to avoid paying more than you need to.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Hotel Shogran rates per night in 2026 range from Rs. 20,500 (Standard Room) to Rs. 28,500 (Luxury Main Block / VIP Executive). All room categories sleep up to 4 guests, and booking requires a 50% advance with free cancellation up to 48 hours before check-in.

Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran Prices Per Night (2026 Rate Card)

Below is the current published tariff for Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran. Every category is priced per room, per night, and accommodates a maximum of four guests.

What the Rs. 20,500 Standard Room Gets You

The Standard Room is the entry point into the property and the answer most travellers are looking for when they search pine park hotel shogran rates per night. It is a genuine four-person room — one double bed plus a sofa bed — with Wi-Fi and hot water. Standard rooms sit in a separate block from the main building, which means a short walk across the lawn to reach the restaurant. For couples or a small family who plan to spend the day at Siri Paye and only return to sleep, this is the smartest value in the property.

The Rs. 24,500–25,500 Middle Tier

The Luxury Room (Rs. 24,500) and VIP Room on the first floor (Rs. 25,500) are the sweet spot for most guests. You gain better finishes, more reliable heating, and — critically in Shogran — a better outlook. The extra Rs. 4,000–5,000 over a Standard Room mostly buys you position: closer to the restaurant, better light, and a window worth waking up to.

The Rs. 28,500 Top Tier

Two categories share the top price point: the Luxury Main Block and the VIP/Executive rooms on the second floor. Both sit inside the main building, so you are steps from dining and reception rather than crossing the grounds in the cold. The second-floor Executive rooms carry the best elevation on the property and are the ones repeat guests request by name.

What Is Included in the Pine Park Shogran Rates?

Understanding what the nightly rate covers is just as important as the number itself. Included with every booking at Pine Park:

  • Free parking — on-site, no separate charge
  • Free Wi-Fi — strongest around reception and the main block
  • Hot water and room heating — essential from October through April
  • Power backup — Shogran load-shedding is a real issue; the generator is not
  • 24-hour security and daily housekeeping
  • Access to the lawns, bonfire area and BBQ facility

Meals are not bundled into the room rate. The on-site restaurant serves fresh local trout and traditional Pakistani food, billed separately. Budget roughly Rs. 3,000–5,000 per person per day for full board if you eat all three meals at the hotel.

Booking Terms That Affect Your Final Price

Three policies materially change what you actually pay:

  1. 50% advance payment is required to confirm the reservation. The balance is settled at the property.
  2. Free cancellation up to 48 hours before check-in. Inside that window, the advance is typically non-refundable — important if you are watching a weather forecast.
  3. Check-in is 1:00 PM and check-out is 12:00 noon. Early check-in on peak weekends is rarely possible because the property runs near full occupancy in July and August.

Is Pine Park Worth the Price in Shogran?

Pine Park is one of the oldest and largest properties in Shogran, occupying more than two acres of lawn, cottages and pine forest. That land is the product — nowhere else in Shogran gives you that much open, maintained green space with Makra Peak in the background. If you are comparing purely on room square footage, cheaper options exist. If you are comparing on grounds, bonfire nights, family space and the view from the lawn, the premium makes sense.

That said, it is worth being clear-eyed. Guest feedback consistently notes that restaurant pricing is on the higher side and that hot water can run on timings during peak occupancy. Rooms facing the mountains are colder at night than those facing the lawn — ask for a lawn-facing room in shoulder season and a mountain-facing one in high summer.

If the tariff sits above your budget, you have solid alternatives within the same valley. Sky View Hotel and Family Resort Shogran and Grand Vista Hotel Shogran both offer comfortable mountain stays at lower entry rates, and you can compare the full inventory on our Shogran hotels page.

How to Get the Best Rate

  • Travel midweek. Sunday to Thursday nights are materially easier to negotiate than Friday and Saturday.
  • Avoid Eid holidays and the 14 August long weekend — these are the two hardest dates of the year in Kaghan.
  • Book two or more rooms together. Family groups taking a cottage block have more leverage than single-room bookings.
  • Consider May, September or October. The valley is green, the crowds are gone, and rates soften. See our full breakdown in the Pine Park Shogran seasonal price guide.
  • Bundle transport. If you are driving up from Islamabad, our rent a car service often works out cheaper than arranging a jeep separately at Kiwai.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the cheapest room at Pine Park Hotel Shogran?

The Standard Room at Rs. 20,500 per night is the lowest published rate. It sleeps up to four guests with one double bed and one sofa bed.

Do Pine Park Shogran prices include breakfast?

No. Room rates are quoted room-only. Meals at the on-site restaurant are charged separately.

How much advance payment is required?

Fifty percent of the total booking value is required in advance to confirm the reservation, with the balance payable at the hotel.

Are children charged extra?

Each room accommodates up to four guests within the quoted rate. Additional guests beyond four, or extra bedding, may attract a supplement — confirm this at the time of booking.

Can I get a refund if I cancel?

Yes, cancellations made more than 48 hours before check-in qualify for free cancellation. Later cancellations are usually non-refundable against the advance.

Ready to Book?

Rates in Kaghan move with the season and with occupancy, so the fastest way to lock a confirmed price for your exact dates is to check availability directly. View live room availability, photos and the booking form on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or call 0343 585 3835.

Planning the wider trip? Pair your stay with a jeep run to the Siri Paye Meadows and browse our curated Shogran and Kaghan tour packages for a ready-made itinerary.

records.title: Pine Park Shogran Price Guide 2026: Peak vs Off-Season Rates
records.content:
The single biggest factor in what you pay for a room in Kaghan is when you go. The same Luxury Room at Pine Park Hotel and Resorts that feels expensive on a July long weekend feels like a bargain on a crisp October Tuesday. This guide explains the Pine Park Shogran price picture season by season, so you can pick dates that match your budget instead of fighting the calendar.

Quick Answer: Published Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran prices per night run from Rs. 20,500 to Rs. 28,500. Peak demand falls between mid-June and late August plus Eid and 14 August holidays. The cheapest realistic windows are late April to mid-May, and mid-September to late October, when the valley is still green but occupancy drops sharply.

The Base Rate Card You Are Working From

Before talking seasons, know the baseline. These are the published per-night rates for 2026:

For a category-by-category explanation of what separates these rooms, read our Pine Park Shogran room types and tariff breakdown.

Shogran’s Travel Calendar, Month by Month

April to Mid-May — The Quiet Green Window

Snow has cleared from the Shogran plateau, the pines are washed clean, and the meadows are turning. Siri Paye may still hold patches of snow at the top, which many travellers actually prefer. Occupancy is low, the jeep track is quieter, and this is one of the two best value windows of the year. Nights are genuinely cold — confirm room heating when you book.

Mid-May to Mid-June — Shoulder Rising

Weekends start to fill but weekdays remain open. This is the last comfortable window before the summer rush. If you want peak-season scenery at shoulder-season ease, target the first two weeks of June, midweek.

Mid-June to End of August — Peak Season

This is when Pakistan moves to the mountains. Expect the property near capacity on weekends, the Kiwai jeep stand busy, and zero flexibility on rates. Book four to six weeks ahead for July and August weekends, and expect to pay the published rate without discount. The upside is that Shogran is at its most spectacular — full green, mild days, and long evenings on the lawn.

The Three Dates to Avoid If You Want Value

  • Eid-ul-Fitr holidays — the valley fills within hours of the moon sighting
  • Eid-ul-Adha holidays — same pattern, plus heavier road traffic on the Kaghan road
  • 14 August long weekend — the single hardest booking date of the Pakistani travel year

On these dates, availability matters more than price. If your travel is fixed to a holiday, book early and treat the published rate as final.

September to Late October — The Best Value in the Year

If we could only recommend one window, this is it. Schools reopen, families go home, and Shogran empties out while staying beautiful. The light is better for photography, the air is cooler, and the jeep track to Siri Paye Meadows is far more pleasant without a convoy ahead of you. Rates soften and negotiation on multi-night stays becomes realistic.

November to March — Snow Season

Shogran under snow is a different destination. Rates drop, but access becomes the variable — the jeep track from Kiwai can require a proper 4×4 and, in heavy snow, may close temporarily. Room heating and hot water become non-negotiable requirements rather than nice-to-haves. If snowfall is the reason you are going, late December through February is the window, and flexibility on dates matters more than a few thousand rupees.

Peak vs Off-Season: What Actually Changes

Six Practical Ways to Lower Your Pine Park Shogran Price

  1. Shift your weekend. Checking in Sunday and out Tuesday instead of Friday to Sunday is the single highest-impact change you can make.
  2. Stay two nights, not one. Longer stays give the property a reason to work with you, and you actually get to see Siri Paye properly instead of rushing it.
  3. Pick the Standard Room and upgrade your food budget. You will spend most daylight hours outside the room anyway.
  4. Confirm what is not included. Meals are billed separately. Knowing this upfront prevents the bill shock that drives most negative reviews.
  5. Compare within the valley. Grand Vista Hotel Shogran and Sky View Hotel Shogran serve a different budget band with genuinely good views — worth checking before you commit.
  6. Handle your own transport. A pre-arranged vehicle through our rent a car service removes the Kiwai jeep-stand markup entirely.

Budgeting a Full Shogran Trip, Not Just the Room

A useful way to think about the total cost of two nights at Pine Park for a family of four:

  • Rooms: Rs. 41,000–57,000 for two nights, depending on category
  • Meals: roughly Rs. 3,000–5,000 per person per day at the on-site restaurant
  • Siri Paye jeep: a per-vehicle charge from Shogran, negotiated locally
  • Fuel and tolls from Islamabad: a six to seven hour drive each way via Mansehra and Balakot

Once you see it laid out, the room is often not the item worth optimising hardest — the season is.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the cheapest month to stay at Pine Park Shogran?

Late April to mid-May and mid-September to late October offer the best combination of low occupancy and good weather. Winter months are cheaper still, but access can be restricted by snow.

Do Pine Park Shogran rates change on weekends?

Weekend demand in peak season is dramatically higher than midweek, so availability tightens and there is no room to negotiate. Midweek stays are consistently easier and more flexible.

How far in advance should I book for July or August?

Four to six weeks for weekend dates. For Eid holidays and 14 August, book as soon as your dates are fixed.

Is Shogran worth visiting in winter?

Yes, if snow is your goal and you are travelling in a capable vehicle. Confirm road and jeep-track conditions before you set out, and make sure your room has working heating.

Lock In Your Dates

The best price at Pine Park is the one attached to the right week. Check live availability and the current rate for your exact dates on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or read the full Pine Park Shogran price and rate card guide for a category-level breakdown. For help building the whole itinerary, browse our Shogran tour packages.

records.title: Pine Park Hotel Shogran Contact Number, Location & Booking Guide
records.content:
If you have been searching for the Pine Park Hotel Shogran contact number, the direct line is 0343 585 3835. This guide gives you the contact details, the exact location, the road route from Islamabad, and a step-by-step booking process — everything you need to go from “we should visit Shogran” to a confirmed reservation.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran can be reached at 0343 585 3835 (call or WhatsApp). The property is located in Shogran, postal code 21230, Mansehra District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, at approximately 2,362 metres above sea level. It is the first major hotel on your left as you arrive from the Kiwai jeep track. Booking requires a 50% advance.

Pine Park Hotel Shogran Contact Details

WhatsApp is generally the faster channel. Mobile coverage on the Shogran plateau is workable but not flawless, and a written message with your dates, room category and guest count gets a cleaner reply than a dropped call.

Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran Location Explained

Shogran is a forested plateau above the Kunhar River in the Kaghan Valley, sitting at roughly 2,362 metres (about 7,750 feet). Pine Park occupies more than two acres of it — lawns, cottage blocks, a main building and standing pine forest. Long-time visitors will tell you it is among the oldest established hotels on the plateau, and its footprint is noticeably larger than the newer properties clustered near Shogran bazaar.

The practical landmark: coming up from Kiwai, Pine Park is the first significant hotel you meet on your left. If you have passed the main bazaar, you have gone too far.

Elevation and What It Means for You

  • Daytime temperatures stay pleasant even in July when the plains are unbearable
  • Nights are cold year-round — pack a jacket even in August
  • Mountain-facing rooms run noticeably colder overnight than lawn-facing rooms
  • Altitude is mild enough that acclimatisation is not a concern for most travellers

How to Reach Pine Park Hotel Shogran

From Islamabad / Rawalpindi

Budget six to seven hours for the drive. The route runs Islamabad → Hazara Motorway (M-15) → Mansehra → Balakot → Kiwai. From Kiwai, a jeep track climbs to the Shogran plateau.

From Lahore

Add roughly four to five hours to the Islamabad timing. Most travellers break the journey at Islamabad or Abbottabad rather than attempting it in one push.

The Kiwai to Shogran Jeep Track

This is the part that surprises first-time visitors. The final climb from Kiwai is a winding unpaved track. In good conditions a capable 4×4 handles it comfortably; a standard sedan should not attempt it. Most travellers park at Kiwai and hire a local jeep for the ascent, which takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes depending on traffic.

Two things worth knowing:

  1. Jeep rates at Kiwai are negotiated locally and rise sharply in peak season. Confirm the price before you load bags.
  2. If you are already in a 4×4, you can usually drive straight up — but check current track conditions, especially after rain or snow.

If you would rather not deal with the Kiwai jeep stand at all, arranging a vehicle in advance through our Shogran rent a car service removes the negotiation and the wait.

How to Book: A Step-by-Step Process

  1. Fix your dates and room category. Rates run from Rs. 20,500 for a Standard Room to Rs. 28,500 for VIP/Executive. See the full Pine Park Shogran price and rate card before you call.
  2. Check availability. Use the live booking form on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts page, or message the hotel directly.
  3. Send your details. Full name, phone, city, check-in and check-out dates, number of guests, number of rooms, and any special request such as a lawn-facing room.
  4. Pay the 50% advance. This is what actually holds the room — a verbal confirmation in peak season is not a booking.
  5. Keep the confirmation message. Screenshot it. Mobile signal on arrival day is not guaranteed.
  6. Arrive after 1:00 PM. Earlier arrivals in July and August are usually asked to wait, because the property runs near full.

What to Ask Before You Confirm

A short list of questions that prevent almost every common complaint:

  • Is the room lawn-facing or mountain-facing?
  • Is room heating provided, and is it included or charged separately?
  • Are there hot water timings, or is it available around the clock?
  • Is the room in the main building or a separate block?
  • What is the current condition of the Kiwai jeep track?
  • Can the hotel arrange a jeep for Siri Paye Meadows, and at what rate?

Nearby Attractions From the Property

Pine Park works well as a base because most of the valley’s highlights are reachable as day trips:

  • Siri Paye Meadows — the reason most people come to Shogran. A short, steep jeep ride to alpine meadows with mirror ponds and Makra Peak behind them.
  • Makra Peak — a popular trek rising above the meadows for those wanting a proper walk.
  • Kawai Waterfall — right on the route up, an easy stop on the way in or out.
  • Sharan Forest — dense old-growth forest, a quieter alternative to the meadows.
  • Naran and Lake Saif-ul-Malook — a longer day trip deeper into Kaghan.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Pine Park Hotel Shogran contact number?

The direct number is 0343 585 3835, available for both calls and WhatsApp. Booking assistance is also available on 0301 087 3333.

Where exactly is Pine Park Hotel and Resorts located?

In Shogran, postal code 21230, Mansehra District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, at approximately 2,362 metres above sea level. It is the first major hotel on your left arriving from Kiwai.

Can I drive my own car to the hotel?

Only in a capable 4×4. The final stretch from Kiwai is an unpaved mountain track. Sedans and small hatchbacks should park at Kiwai and hire a jeep.

How long is the drive from Islamabad to Shogran?

Roughly six to seven hours via Mansehra and Balakot, plus 30 to 45 minutes for the jeep climb from Kiwai.

What are the check-in and check-out times?

Check-in is 1:00 PM and check-out is 12:00 noon. Free cancellation applies up to 48 hours before check-in.

Is there mobile signal and Wi-Fi at the hotel?

Free Wi-Fi is provided, strongest near reception and the main block. Mobile coverage on the plateau is workable but can be patchy in poor weather.

Book Your Stay

Have your dates ready and call 0343 585 3835, or use the live availability form on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page. If you are still comparing properties, our full Shogran hotels directory lists every option on the plateau with current rates.

records.title: Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran Photos: Rooms, Views & Property Tour
records.content:
Photographs settle arguments that price lists cannot. This is a full visual walkthrough of Pine Park Hotel & Resort Shogran — the grounds, every room category, the views from each side of the property, and what the place actually looks like when you step out of the jeep. If you are deciding between rooms, scroll slowly.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Hotel and Resort Shogran spans more than two acres of maintained lawn and pine forest at 2,362 metres. The property offers five room categories across a main building and separate blocks, with rooms facing either the lawn or the mountains. Lawn-facing rooms get morning sun; mountain-facing rooms get the Makra Peak outlook and colder nights.

First Impression: The Grounds

The thing photographs of Shogran hotels usually fail to convey is scale. Pine Park is not a building with a garden — it is a piece of land with buildings on it. The lawn runs wide and open, edged by standing pine, with the mountains rising directly behind. On a clear morning the mist burns off the treeline and the whole plateau opens up.

This is also where the bonfire and BBQ evenings happen — consistently the highlight guests mention. It is a genuinely social space, which is unusual in Shogran where most properties are compact.

Standard Room — Rs. 20,500 Per Night

The Standard Rooms sit in a block separate from the main building. Practically, that means a short walk across the grounds to reach the restaurant — pleasant in June, less so at 7 AM in November. The room itself is honest and functional: a double bed, a sofa bed, warm wooden tones, hot water and Wi-Fi.

For travellers who plan to spend the day at Siri Paye Meadows and only use the room to sleep, this is the sensible pick.

Luxury Room — Rs. 24,500 Per Night

A clear step up in finish. Better light, more considered furnishing, and the kind of room that photographs well without needing a flattering angle.

Luxury Main Block — Rs. 28,500 Per Night

The Main Block rooms are inside the primary building. The advantage is entirely practical and entirely real: you are steps from the restaurant, reception and the strongest Wi-Fi signal on the property. In cold months, not crossing open ground to get dinner is worth more than most people expect.

VIP Room, First Floor — Rs. 25,500 Per Night

Elevation changes everything in a mountain property. First-floor VIP rooms lift you above the immediate treeline and open up the outlook considerably compared to ground-level rooms at the same finish level.

VIP / Executive, Second Floor — Rs. 28,500 Per Night

The top of the property, literally and in tariff. These are the rooms repeat guests ask for by name, and the reason is the view. Second-floor Executive rooms give you the widest sightline across the lawn to the peaks beyond.

Which View Should You Ask For?

This is the most useful thing in this article, and it comes straight from guest experience rather than a brochure.

The short rule: book lawn-facing in cold months, mountain-facing in high summer. Getting this one decision right does more for your stay than upgrading a room category.

What the Photos Do Not Show

Honest context matters as much as a good gallery. A few things worth setting expectations on:

  • The approach road. The final climb from Kiwai is an unpaved jeep track. It is part of the experience, but it is not smooth.
  • Hot water timings. During high occupancy, hot water may run on schedule rather than around the clock. Ask when booking.
  • Restaurant pricing. Meals are billed separately and sit at the higher end. Budget for it.
  • Wi-Fi coverage. Reliable near reception and the main block, weaker in the outer cottage blocks.

For the full picture including guest feedback, read our honest Pine Park Shogran review.

Best Photo Spots on the Property

If photographs are part of why you are coming, these are the four locations worth planning around:

  1. The centre of the lawn, facing the peaks. Wide open foreground, pine boundary, mountains behind. Best around 7 to 8 AM before the light goes flat.
  2. The pine boundary looking back at the property. Puts the buildings in scale against the forest — the shot that actually communicates how large Pine Park is.
  3. From a second-floor Executive window. Elevation gives you a sightline that ground-level rooms simply cannot match, especially when mist is sitting in the valley.
  4. The bonfire area after dark. Warm light against a very dark mountain sky. Bring something that handles low light, or lean into the silhouettes.

One practical note on timing: Kaghan afternoons cloud over frequently. Peaks that are crisp at 8 AM are often invisible by 2 PM. If a clear-mountain photograph matters to you, shoot it the moment you see it rather than planning it for later.

What the Property Looks Like Across the Seasons

For a full breakdown of when to travel and what it costs, see our Pine Park Shogran seasonal price guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many room categories does Pine Park Shogran have?

Five published categories: Standard Room, Luxury Room, VIP Room (1st Floor), Luxury Main Block, and VIP/Executive (2nd Floor). All accommodate up to four guests.

Which Pine Park Shogran room has the best view?

The VIP/Executive rooms on the second floor offer the widest outlook across the lawn toward the surrounding peaks.

How big is the property?

More than two acres, comprising lawns, cottage blocks, a main building, restaurant, bonfire area and standing pine forest.

Are the rooms heated?

Room heating is listed among the property amenities. Confirm availability and whether it is included for your specific room at the time of booking, especially for winter stays.

See It in Person

Photos get you most of the way there; a confirmed booking gets you the rest. Browse the complete gallery, live availability and current rates on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or compare against every other property on the plateau in our Shogran hotels directory.

records.title: Pine Park Resort Shogran: Facilities, Amenities & Services (2026)
records.content:
A mountain hotel lives or dies on its facilities. At 2,362 metres, “does the hot water work” is not a luxury question — it is the difference between a memorable trip and a miserable one. This is a complete, practical rundown of every amenity at Pine Park Resort Shogran, what works well, and what you should confirm before you arrive.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Resort Shogran offers free Wi-Fi, free parking, an on-site restaurant, room service, power backup, hot water, room heating, TV/cable, gardens, a bonfire area, BBQ facilities, laundry, 24-hour security, family rooms and jeep arrangements for Siri Paye. The property spans over two acres with mountain and valley views.

The Complete Amenity List

Utilities: The Ones That Actually Matter in Shogran

Power Backup

Load-shedding in Kaghan is real and unpredictable. Pine Park runs power backup, which in practice means your lights, charging and heating are not hostage to the grid. For a multi-day stay with phones, cameras and possibly a power bank for the Siri Paye trip, this is the single most valuable utility on the list.

Hot Water

Hot water is provided. The honest caveat, reflected consistently in guest feedback, is that during high occupancy it may run on timings rather than around the clock. Mornings are generally reliable. If you are travelling in winter or with young children, ask about current timings when you book — a two-minute question that prevents the most common complaint about mountain properties across the whole valley.

Room Heating

Room heating is listed among the property amenities. Shogran nights are cold in every season — genuinely cold from October to April, and cool enough for a jacket even in August. Mountain-facing rooms run colder overnight than lawn-facing ones, so heating matters more on that side of the property. Confirm heating for your specific room category at the time of booking.

Dining and the Restaurant

The on-site restaurant serves fresh local trout and traditional Pakistani cuisine. Room service is available. Two things to plan around:

  • Meals are not included in the room rate. Budget roughly Rs. 3,000–5,000 per person per day for full board.
  • Restaurant pricing sits at the higher end for the valley, and portion sizes draw mixed feedback. Some guests prefer to eat one meal daily in Shogran bazaar and use the hotel for breakfast and dinner.

The BBQ and bonfire evenings, however, get near-universal praise. If your stay includes a Saturday night, ask about arranging one — a well-run BBQ dinner on the lawn under Kaghan’s sky is the memory most guests carry home.

The Grounds: Pine Park’s Real Differentiator

More than two acres of maintained lawn, flower beds, standing pine and open space. In a valley where most properties are compact buildings on small plots, this is what separates Pine Park. Practically it means:

  • Children can actually run around without being on a road
  • Group and family gatherings work — cottage blocks can be taken together
  • Gentle forest walks start at your door, no vehicle required
  • Photography is easy — the lawn framed by pine with peaks behind is the shot everyone comes for

Family-Specific Facilities

Pine Park is structurally a family property. Every room category accommodates up to four guests with a double bed plus a sofa bed, so a family of four fits into a single room without an extra-bed negotiation. Combined with the open grounds, 24-hour security and daily housekeeping, it removes most of the friction that makes mountain travel with children difficult.

If you are travelling with a larger group, taking multiple rooms in the same block keeps everyone together — worth requesting explicitly when booking rather than assuming.

Travel Services: Getting to Siri Paye

The resort can arrange jeep transport for the run up to Siri Paye Meadows, which is the primary reason most people base themselves in Shogran. Rates are negotiated locally and rise in peak season, so agree the price before departure.

If you would rather have transport sorted before you leave home — including the drive up from Islamabad and the Kiwai ascent — our Shogran rent a car service handles the whole chain, and our Kaghan tour packages bundle it with accommodation.

What Pine Park Does Not Have

Honest expectation-setting prevents disappointment. This is a mountain resort in northern Pakistan, not a city five-star. There is no pool, no spa, and no gym. Wi-Fi is strongest at reception and the main block, weaker in the outer cottages. Mobile signal on the plateau is workable but not guaranteed in bad weather. And the approach is an unpaved jeep track — the isolation that makes Shogran beautiful is the same isolation that limits what any property here can offer.

If a specific amenity is critical to your trip, compare across the plateau first. Sky View Hotel and Family Resort Shogran and Grand Vista Hotel Shogran are the closest comparable options, and the full list is on our Shogran hotels page.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Pine Park Resort Shogran have Wi-Fi?

Yes, free Wi-Fi is provided. Coverage is strongest near reception and the main building and weaker in outlying cottage blocks.

Is parking free at Pine Park Shogran?

Yes, on-site parking is free. Note that the final approach from Kiwai requires a 4×4; many guests park at Kiwai and take a jeep up.

Does the hotel have a generator?

Power backup is provided, which covers the frequent load-shedding in the Kaghan region.

Is food included in the room rate?

No. The room rate is quoted room-only, and meals at the on-site restaurant are billed separately.

Can Pine Park arrange a jeep for Siri Paye?

Yes, jeep transport to Siri Paye Meadows can be arranged through the property. Confirm the rate before you set off, as prices vary with season.

Are there family rooms?

Every room category sleeps up to four guests with one double bed and one sofa bed, and family rooms are among the listed amenities.

Check Live Availability

Amenities are only useful on dates you can actually book. See current rates, full facility details and live availability on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or review the complete Pine Park Shogran price breakdown before you decide on a category.

records.title: Pine Park Hotel and Resort Shogran: Complete Honest Review 2026
records.content:
Most reviews of Pine Park Hotel and Resort Shogran are either a brochure or a rant. This one is neither. Below is a balanced assessment based on the property’s published details and the recurring themes in years of guest feedback — what Pine Park genuinely does better than anything else in Shogran, and where it falls short of the price it charges.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Hotel and Resort Shogran is the largest and among the oldest established properties in Shogran, with over two acres of lawn and pine forest. Rooms run Rs. 20,500–28,500 per night. Its strengths are the grounds, the family setup and the bonfire evenings. Its weaknesses are restaurant pricing, occasional hot water timings, and inconsistency between room categories. Overall verdict: strong for families and groups, less compelling for solo budget travellers.

The Verdict in One Paragraph

Pine Park is not the newest hotel in Shogran and it is not the cheapest. What it has, that no newer property can replicate, is land. Over two acres of maintained lawn, cottage blocks and standing pine, with the mountains behind. If your trip is about the grounds — children running on grass, a bonfire in the evening, a family gathering that needs space — Pine Park is the correct answer in Shogran. If your trip is about a modern room at a keen price, look elsewhere.

What Pine Park Gets Right

1. The Grounds Are Genuinely Exceptional

This is the recurring theme in almost every positive review, and it holds up. The lawns are well maintained, the pine boundary is real forest rather than landscaping, and the open space transforms what a mountain stay feels like. Compact properties near Shogran bazaar simply cannot offer this.

2. It Works Properly for Families

Every room category takes four guests — a double bed plus a sofa bed — so a family of four fits into one room without an extra-bed conversation. Add 24-hour security, safe open space away from the road, and the ability to book adjacent cottages for a larger group, and the practical friction of travelling with children drops considerably.

3. Bonfire and BBQ Evenings

Consistently the most-praised element of the experience. A well-run BBQ on the lawn, with the cold coming down off the peaks and a fire going, is what guests describe when they recommend the place to friends.

4. Location on the Plateau

Coming up from Kiwai, Pine Park is the first major hotel on your left — you are not fighting through bazaar traffic with luggage. It also sits well positioned for the jeep run to Siri Paye Meadows, the main reason most people come to Shogran at all.

Where Pine Park Falls Short

1. Restaurant Pricing and Value

The most common criticism, by a wide margin. The restaurant is priced at the higher end for the valley, and feedback on portion size relative to cost is mixed. The food itself — particularly the local trout — draws better reviews than the billing does. Practical workaround: budget realistically for meals, or take one meal a day in Shogran bazaar.

2. Hot Water Timings

Hot water is provided, but during peak occupancy it can run on schedule rather than around the clock. In a location this cold, that is a meaningful issue. Ask about current timings at the time of booking.

3. Inconsistency Between Room Categories

This is the most useful thing to know before you book. The gap between Standard Rooms and the Main Block or Executive categories is larger than the Rs. 8,000 price difference suggests. Standard Rooms sit in a separate block, requiring a walk across the grounds to reach the restaurant, and reviewers describe them as functional rather than impressive. The upper categories inside the main building draw noticeably warmer feedback.

Recommendation: if your budget allows, the Luxury Room at Rs. 24,500 or the VIP first floor at Rs. 25,500 is the best value point on the tariff. Full category detail is in our Pine Park room types and tariff guide.

4. Service Is Variable

Feedback on staff ranges from warm praise to genuine frustration, which usually indicates a property that performs well at moderate occupancy and struggles at full. This is not unusual in Kaghan during July and August. Travelling midweek or in shoulder season materially improves the service experience.

5. The Approach Road

Not the hotel’s fault, but worth stating plainly: the final climb from Kiwai is an unpaved jeep track requiring a 4×4. First-time visitors in a sedan are regularly caught out. Park at Kiwai and hire a jeep, or arrange a suitable vehicle in advance through our rent a car service.

The Room Choice That Changes Your Review

More than any other decision, view orientation determines whether guests come away happy:

  • Lawn-facing rooms — warmer at night, sunny in the morning, more activity and noise. Best in spring, autumn and winter.
  • Mountain-facing rooms — significantly colder overnight, quieter, better outlook. Best in peak summer.

Guests who book a mountain-facing room in October and then complain about the cold are, in a sense, reviewing their own booking. Ask for orientation explicitly.

Who Should Book Pine Park — and Who Should Not

How It Compares in Shogran

Pine Park sits at the upper end of Shogran’s tariff range. If the rate is above your budget, Sky View Hotel and Family Resort Shogran and Grand Vista Hotel Shogran both deliver strong mountain views at lower entry rates, and Pine Wood Hotel and Family Cottage Malakandi is worth considering if you are open to staying deeper in the valley. Compare all options side by side on our Shogran hotels directory.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Pine Park Hotel Shogran worth the money?

For families and groups who will use the grounds, yes — nothing else in Shogran offers comparable space. For solo travellers or those who mainly want a modern room, the value case is weaker.

What is the biggest complaint about Pine Park Shogran?

Restaurant pricing relative to portion size is the most frequently raised issue, followed by hot water running on timings during peak occupancy.

Which room category should I book?

The Luxury Room (Rs. 24,500) or VIP first floor (Rs. 25,500) offers the best balance. Standard Rooms at Rs. 20,500 are functional but sit in a separate block.

Is Pine Park good for children?

Yes. The open lawns, family room configuration and 24-hour security make it one of the better family choices in the Kaghan Valley.

How old is the property?

Pine Park is among the longest-established hotels on the Shogran plateau, and has been progressively renovated over the years.

Make Your Own Judgement

Reviews narrow the field; your dates decide it. Check live availability, current rates and the full photo gallery on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or see the complete visual walkthrough in our Pine Park Shogran photo tour.

records.title: Shogran Pine Park: Why It Is Rated the Best Hotel in Shogran
records.content:
Shogran has a growing list of hotels, but one name comes up before all the others. Ask anyone who has been, and the answer is Shogran Pine Park. This guide explains why — and, just as importantly, when a different property on the plateau might suit you better.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Hotel and Resorts is the most recommended hotel in Shogran because of its scale — over two acres of lawn and pine forest, five room categories from Rs. 20,500 to Rs. 28,500, family rooms sleeping four, bonfire and BBQ facilities, and a prime position as the first major hotel arriving from Kiwai. It suits families and groups best; budget solo travellers may prefer smaller properties.

What Makes a Hotel “Best” in Shogran?

Shogran is a small plateau at roughly 2,362 metres in the Kaghan Valley. Almost every hotel here has a decent view — that is not a differentiator. What genuinely separates properties is a shorter list:

  1. Land. How much usable outdoor space does the property actually own?
  2. Utilities. Power backup, hot water and heating are not luxuries at this altitude.
  3. Family capacity. Can four people sleep in one room without a negotiation?
  4. Position. How much bazaar traffic do you fight with luggage?
  5. Access to Siri Paye. Can the property put you in a jeep without a hassle?

Measured against those five, Pine Park wins on four and ties on the fifth.

Reason 1: Nothing Else Has the Land

Pine Park occupies more than two acres of maintained lawn, cottage blocks, flower beds and standing pine. Most Shogran hotels are a building on a compact plot. This single difference reshapes the entire stay — children have somewhere to be, groups have somewhere to gather, and the bonfire has somewhere to happen.

It is also the reason the property photographs so well: open green foreground, pine boundary, peaks behind. See the full walkthrough in our Pine Park Shogran photo tour.

Reason 2: Five Room Categories, One Budget Range

Every category sleeps up to four with a double bed and a sofa bed. That flexibility matters: a family can trade down to a Standard Room without losing capacity, or trade up for position without changing hotels.

Reason 3: It Is Built for Families

Family rooms, open and secure grounds, 24-hour security, daily housekeeping, and the ability to book adjacent cottages for extended family. Shogran attracts a lot of family travel from Islamabad, Rawalpindi and Lahore, and Pine Park is structurally set up for it in a way that newer, smaller properties are not.

Reason 4: The Utilities Hold Up

Power backup for Kaghan’s load-shedding, hot water, room heating, free Wi-Fi and free parking. At 2,362 metres these are the amenities that determine whether you enjoy the trip. The honest caveat: hot water can run on timings during peak occupancy, so confirm current schedules when you book. Full detail is in our Pine Park Shogran facilities guide.

Reason 5: Position and Siri Paye Access

Arriving from Kiwai, Pine Park is the first major hotel on your left — before the bazaar congestion. From there, the jeep run to Siri Paye Meadows is straightforward, and the property can arrange transport. Given that Siri Paye is why most people choose Shogran over Naran in the first place, this convenience carries real weight.

When Pine Park Is Not the Right Answer

A fair guide has to include this. Consider other options if:

  • You are travelling solo or as a couple on a tight budget. You will pay for grounds you have limited use for.
  • You want a modern, boutique-style room. Pine Park is an established property with progressive renovation, not a new build.
  • You expect city five-star service. Service quality varies with occupancy, particularly on July and August weekends.
  • You want to eat cheaply on site. Restaurant pricing sits at the higher end and meals are billed separately.

In those cases, look at Sky View Hotel and Family Resort Shogran or Grand Vista Hotel Shogran, both of which offer strong mountain views at lower entry rates. If you are open to staying deeper in Kaghan, Pine Wood Hotel Malakandi and Parbat View Hotel Paras widen the field further.

Shogran Hotel Comparison at a Glance

Planning the Rest of Your Shogran Trip

Wherever you stay, build in at least two nights. A single night means arriving tired from a six to seven hour drive, rushing Siri Paye, and leaving. Two nights lets you do the meadows properly and still have a morning on the lawn.

Worth adding to the itinerary:

  • Siri Paye Meadows — the essential half-day jeep trip
  • Sharan Forest — dense old-growth forest, far quieter than the meadows
  • Manna Meadows — an alternative for travellers wanting to avoid crowds
  • Kawai Waterfall — an easy stop on the way up or down
  • Naran and Lake Saif-ul-Malook — a longer day trip north

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is the best hotel in Shogran?

Pine Park Hotel and Resorts is the most widely recommended, primarily for its two-plus acres of grounds, family room configuration and bonfire facilities. Sky View and Grand Vista are strong alternatives at lower rates.

How much does Shogran Pine Park cost per night?

From Rs. 20,500 for a Standard Room up to Rs. 28,500 for VIP/Executive, with all categories sleeping up to four guests.

Is Pine Park the oldest hotel in Shogran?

It is among the longest-established properties on the plateau and has been renovated progressively over the years.

How many nights should I stay in Shogran?

Two nights is the minimum that makes the drive worthwhile and allows a proper Siri Paye trip without rushing.

Book the Best Room, Not Just the Best Hotel

Choosing Pine Park is step one; choosing the right category and orientation is step two. Check live availability and current rates on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or browse every property on the plateau in our Shogran hotels directory. For a fully arranged trip, see our Shogran and Kaghan tour packages.

records.title: Pine View Hotel Shogran vs Pine Park: Which One Should You Book?
records.content:
Search for Pine View Hotel Shogran and you will find a surprising amount of confusion. Some travellers are looking for a specific property; many more are half-remembering the name of Shogran’s best-known hotel, Pine Park Hotel and Resorts. This guide clears up the naming, then gives you a practical framework for choosing between the pine-named options on the plateau.

Quick Answer: “Pine View Hotel Shogran,” “Pine Hotel Shogran” and “Pine Resort Shogran” are commonly typed variations of Pine Park Hotel and Resorts, the largest and best-known hotel on the Shogran plateau, with rates from Rs. 20,500 to Rs. 28,500 per night. Always confirm the exact property name, address and contact number before paying any advance.

Why the Name Confusion Happens

Shogran sits in dense pine forest, so “pine” appears in a lot of property names across the Kaghan Valley. Travellers remember the pine, not the second word. The result is a cluster of near-identical searches — pine view, pine hotel, pine resort, pine park — that mostly resolve to the same destination.

There is a practical risk here worth naming: if you are booking on the basis of a half-remembered name, you can end up paying an advance to a property that is not the one you saw photographs of. Confirm three things before any payment:

  1. The full, exact property name
  2. The address and postal code — Pine Park is at Shogran, 21230, Mansehra District, KP
  3. The contact number — Pine Park’s direct line is 0343 585 3835

The Property Most People Actually Mean

Pine Park Hotel and Resorts occupies more than two acres on the Shogran plateau — lawns, cottage blocks, a main building, restaurant and standing pine forest. Arriving from Kiwai, it is the first major hotel on your left. It is among the longest-established properties in Shogran and, by some distance, the largest.

Full details are on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts page, and the category-by-category breakdown is in our room types and tariff guide.

A Framework for Choosing Any Shogran Hotel

Rather than chasing a name, choose on criteria. These six questions separate the good bookings from the regrettable ones:

1. How much outdoor space does the property own?

In Shogran, this is the biggest single differentiator. Pine Park’s two-plus acres is the outlier; most properties are compact. If you are travelling with children or a group, land matters more than room finish.

2. Is the room lawn-facing or mountain-facing?

Mountain-facing rooms are significantly colder overnight but quieter with a better outlook. Lawn-facing rooms warm up in the morning sun and sit closer to the social hub. Ask explicitly — this decision affects your stay more than a category upgrade.

3. Power backup, hot water, heating?

Load-shedding in Kaghan is routine. Hot water may run on timings during peak occupancy at any property here. Heating is essential from October through April. Confirm all three.

4. Where is the room relative to the restaurant?

At Pine Park, Standard Rooms sit in a block separate from the main building, meaning a walk across the grounds for meals. Pleasant in June, less so in January. Main Block and Executive rooms avoid this.

5. What is the food arrangement?

Room rates in Shogran are generally quoted room-only. At Pine Park, restaurant pricing sits at the higher end — budget roughly Rs. 3,000–5,000 per person per day for full board, or plan one meal daily in Shogran bazaar.

6. Can they arrange the Siri Paye jeep?

Most people come to Shogran for Siri Paye Meadows. A property that can put you in a jeep without a bazaar negotiation saves genuine time in peak season.

The Realistic Alternatives on the Plateau

If Pine Park’s rates sit above your budget, or it is sold out on your dates, these are the properties genuinely worth comparing:

  • Sky View Hotel and Family Resort Shogran — a family-oriented option with strong views at a lower entry rate.
  • Grand Vista Hotel Shogran — comfortable rooms and a good position on the plateau.
  • Pine Wood Hotel and Family Cottage Malakandi — another pine-named property, but located at Malakandi rather than Shogran. A useful base if you are heading deeper toward Naran.
  • Parbat View Hotel and River Restaurant Paras — riverside, lower in the valley, good for a break in the journey.

Compare current rates for all of them on our Shogran hotels directory.

Note on Pine Wood vs Pine Park

These two are the pair most often confused, and the difference is geography, not just name. Pine Park is on the Shogran plateau — the base for Siri Paye. Pine Wood is at Malakandi, further along the Kaghan Valley. If your itinerary centres on Siri Paye, you want Shogran. If you are heading toward Naran and Lake Saif-ul-Malook, staying deeper in the valley can make more sense.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Pine View Hotel Shogran the same as Pine Park?

Most searches for “Pine View Hotel Shogran” are looking for Pine Park Hotel and Resorts, the plateau’s largest and best-known property. Always verify the exact name, address and phone number before paying an advance.

What is the difference between Pine Park and Pine Wood?

Location. Pine Park is in Shogran, the base for Siri Paye Meadows. Pine Wood Hotel and Family Cottage is at Malakandi, further along the Kaghan Valley.

How do I avoid booking the wrong Shogran hotel?

Confirm the full property name, the address with postal code, and the direct contact number before transferring any advance payment. Booking through a verified directory removes most of this risk.

Which pine-named hotel in Shogran has the best grounds?

Pine Park Hotel and Resorts, with more than two acres of lawn and pine forest — the largest outdoor footprint on the plateau.

What is the cheapest pine-named option in Shogran?

Pine Park’s Standard Room at Rs. 20,500 is its entry rate. Lower entry rates are available at Sky View and Grand Vista.

Book With Confidence

The safest way to avoid a naming mix-up is to book from a verified listing with a confirmed address and contact number. See the full profile, live rates and booking form on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, or read our honest review of Pine Park before deciding.

records.title: Pine Park Glade Resort Shogran: The Perfect Base for a Siri Paye Trip
records.content:
Almost everyone who books a hotel in Shogran is really booking access to one place: the alpine meadows of Siri and Paye. This guide covers Pine Park Glade Resort Shogran and the wider Pine Park presence on the plateau, and — more usefully — how to use a Shogran base to do the Siri Paye trip properly instead of rushing it.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Glade Resort Shogran is a mountain property in the Shogran area of the Kaghan Valley offering continental breakfast, free Wi-Fi, free parking, a firepit and garden seating with 24-hour room service. It sits close to the Shogran plateau, making it a workable base for the Siri Paye Meadows jeep trip. The larger, longer-established Pine Park Hotel and Resorts is the better-known option with rates from Rs. 20,500 per night.

Pine Park Glade Resort vs Pine Park Hotel and Resorts

First, the naming. These are related but distinct listings, and travellers regularly conflate them.

If you want the property with the big lawns and the bonfire evenings that Shogran is known for, that is Pine Park Hotel and Resorts. Before paying any advance on either, confirm the exact property name, address and contact number — see our guide on avoiding Shogran hotel name confusion.

Why Shogran Is the Right Base for Siri Paye

Siri Paye is reachable only by jeep from Shogran. Staying in Naran and day-tripping to Siri Paye means a long drive before you even start the jeep climb. Staying on the plateau means you can leave early, beat the convoy, and be back by lunch.

The advantages of an early start are not marginal:

  • Light. Morning light on the meadows is dramatically better than midday for photographs.
  • Queues. The Kiwai and Shogran jeep stands back up badly from mid-morning in July and August.
  • Weather. Kaghan afternoons cloud over frequently. Peaks visible at 8 AM are often gone by 2 PM.
  • The walk. Jeeps stop short of the best viewpoints. You want time and energy to walk the last stretch.

Planning the Siri Paye Day Trip

Getting There

The route to Siri Paye Meadows is a jeep track climbing from the Shogran plateau. It is steep, unpaved and only for 4×4 vehicles — this is not a drive you attempt in your own sedan. Most properties, including Pine Park, can arrange a jeep. Rates are negotiated locally and rise sharply in peak season, so agree the price before you set off.

What You Will Find

Siri is the lower meadow with a small pond; Paye is the higher, wider expanse of alpine grassland. On a clear day, Makra Peak rises behind it. In early season there may still be snow patches at the top, which many travellers prefer to the full summer green.

What to Take

  • A warm layer — it is meaningfully colder up there than at the hotel
  • Proper shoes — the ground is uneven and often wet
  • Water and snacks — options at the top are limited and expensive
  • Cash — jeep fares, tea stalls and horse rides are cash-only
  • Sun protection — high-altitude sun burns faster than you expect

Timing

Leave your hotel by 7:30 AM in peak season. The round trip including time at the top runs roughly four to five hours. Afternoons are for the lawn, not the meadows.

Beyond Siri Paye: Filling a Second Day

A two-night stay gives you a full day beyond the meadows. Good options from a Shogran base:

  • Sharan Forest — dense old-growth forest, far quieter than Siri Paye and a genuinely different landscape.
  • Manna Meadows — an alternative meadow trip for travellers who want to avoid the crowds entirely.
  • Makra Peak trek — a serious walk rising above the meadows, for those with a proper day and reasonable fitness.
  • Kawai Waterfall — an easy stop on the way in or out, right on the route.
  • Naran and Lake Saif-ul-Malook — a longer day trip deeper into Kaghan if you have the appetite for more driving.

Getting to Shogran in the First Place

From Islamabad, budget six to seven hours via the Hazara Motorway, Mansehra and Balakot to Kiwai. From Kiwai, the jeep climb to the plateau takes roughly 30 to 45 minutes.

Sedans should park at Kiwai and hire a jeep up. If you would rather not negotiate at the jeep stand after a long drive, arranging a capable vehicle in advance through our Shogran rent a car service handles the whole chain, and our Kaghan tour packages bundle transport with accommodation and the Siri Paye run.

Choosing Your Base: A Practical Comparison

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Pine Park Glade Resort Shogran?

It is a mountain resort listing in the Shogran area of the Kaghan Valley, Mansehra District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Confirm the exact address directly with the property before booking, as several Pine Park listings exist in the area.

Does Pine Park Glade Resort include breakfast?

Continental breakfast is listed as included, along with free Wi-Fi, free parking and 24-hour room service. This differs from Pine Park Hotel and Resorts, where meals are billed separately.

How far is Siri Paye from Shogran?

It is a short but steep jeep ride from the Shogran plateau. Allow four to five hours for the full round trip including time at the meadows.

Can I drive my own car to Siri Paye?

No, unless you have a capable 4×4 and experience on unpaved mountain tracks. Most visitors hire a local jeep.

What is the best time of day to visit Siri Paye?

Early morning. Leave by 7:30 AM in peak season for better light, fewer queues and a much higher chance of clear peak views.

Build Your Shogran Trip

Pick the base first, then the meadows will take care of themselves. Compare live rates and availability on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts page, browse every option on our Shogran hotels directory, or read our seasonal price guide to pick the right week to travel.

records.title: Pine Park Hotel Shogran Room Types & Tariff Breakdown 2026
records.content:
Five room categories, a Rs. 8,000 spread between the cheapest and the most expensive, and all of them sleeping four people. So what exactly are you paying for? This is a detailed breakdown of every Pine Park Hotel Shogran room type, what separates them, and which one is right for your trip.

Quick Answer: Pine Park Hotel Shogran offers five room categories: Standard Room (Rs. 20,500), Luxury Room (Rs. 24,500), VIP Room 1st Floor (Rs. 25,500), Luxury Main Block (Rs. 28,500) and VIP/Executive 2nd Floor (Rs. 28,500). Every category sleeps up to four guests with one double bed and one sofa bed. The main differences are building location, floor level, finish quality and view orientation.

The Full Tariff at a Glance

The critical insight: capacity does not change with price. A family of four fits in the Rs. 20,500 room just as it does in the Rs. 28,500 room. What you buy with the extra money is position and finish, not space for more people.

Standard Room — Rs. 20,500

What you get: A functional four-person room with a double bed, sofa bed, Wi-Fi and hot water.

The trade-off: Standard Rooms sit in a block separate from the main building. Reaching the restaurant means walking across the grounds — pleasant on a June evening, considerably less so at breakfast in November.

Book this if: You are on a budget, travelling in warmer months, and plan to spend your days at Siri Paye Meadows rather than in the room.

Luxury Room — Rs. 24,500

What you get: A clear step up in finish, furnishing and light for Rs. 4,000 more than Standard.

The trade-off: Still outside the main building, so the walk to the restaurant remains.

Book this if: You want the best value on the tariff. For most travellers this is the right answer — the jump in quality from Standard is more noticeable than the jump from Luxury to Main Block.

VIP Room, 1st Floor — Rs. 25,500

What you get: Elevation. In a mountain property, being above the immediate treeline changes the outlook substantially.

The trade-off: Stairs, and only Rs. 1,000 below the Main Block price point.

Book this if: The view matters more to you than proximity to the restaurant, and the Executive rooms are unavailable.

Luxury Main Block — Rs. 28,500

What you get: A room inside the main building — steps from the restaurant, reception and the strongest Wi-Fi on the property.

The trade-off: More activity and noise than the outer blocks.

Book this if: You are travelling in cold months, with elderly guests or very young children, or simply do not want to cross open ground for every meal. In winter this convenience is worth more than the price difference suggests.

VIP / Executive, 2nd Floor — Rs. 28,500

What you get: The best outlook on the property, combined with main-building convenience. Same price as the Main Block but a floor higher.

The trade-off: These book out first in peak season, and there are stairs.

Book this if: You are paying Rs. 28,500 anyway. At an identical rate to the Main Block, the extra elevation makes the Executive the better buy — request it explicitly.

The Decision That Matters More Than Category

Before you agonise over Luxury versus VIP, settle this: lawn-facing or mountain-facing?

Guests who book mountain-facing in October and then find the room freezing are, in effect, reviewing their own choice. State your preference when booking.

What Every Category Includes

  • Free Wi-Fi and free parking
  • Hot water and room heating
  • Power backup for Kaghan load-shedding
  • TV / cable and daily housekeeping
  • Access to lawns, bonfire area and BBQ facility
  • 24-hour security

Not included: meals. The on-site restaurant bills separately, so budget roughly Rs. 3,000–5,000 per person per day for full board. Full amenity detail is in our Pine Park Shogran facilities guide.

Booking Terms

  • Check-in: 1:00 PM  |  Check-out: 12:00 noon
  • Advance: 50% of booking value confirms the room
  • Cancellation: free up to 48 hours before check-in

The Cost Maths: What Each Upgrade Actually Buys

Across a two-night stay, the difference between the cheapest and most expensive category is Rs. 16,000. Set against a six to seven hour drive from Islamabad and everything else the trip costs, most travellers find the mid-tier upgrade the easiest money they spend.

A Quick Way to Decide

  • Travelling in July or August, on a budget, out all day? Standard Room.
  • Want the best balance of price and quality? Luxury Room.
  • Coming for the views and photography? VIP Executive, second floor.
  • Travelling in winter, or with elderly parents or a toddler? Main Block — not crossing open ground for meals is worth the money.
  • Booking two rooms for one family? Ask for both in the same block rather than assuming it happens automatically.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which Pine Park Shogran room type is the best value?

The Luxury Room at Rs. 24,500. The quality jump from Standard is larger than the jump from Luxury to the top categories.

Do more expensive rooms sleep more people?

No. Every category accommodates up to four guests with one double bed and one sofa bed. Higher rates buy position and finish, not capacity.

What is the difference between Luxury Main Block and VIP Executive?

Both are Rs. 28,500. The Main Block is in the main building; the Executive rooms are on the second floor with a wider outlook. At the same price, the Executive is generally the stronger pick.

Can I request a specific room?

Yes. Specify both the category and your view preference at the time of booking, ideally in writing on WhatsApp.

Are extra beds available?

Rooms are configured for four guests. For additional guests or bedding, confirm availability and any supplement directly with the property.

Pick Your Room

Check live availability by category and current rates on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page. For seasonal timing, see our peak vs off-season price guide, or view every category in our Pine Park Shogran photo tour before you decide.

records.title: Pine Park Hotel: Shogran, Naran & Kaghan Locations Explained
records.content:
Search for Pine Park Hotel and you will find listings across Shogran, Naran and the wider Kaghan Valley, plus several near-identical names. This guide untangles the Pine Park name, explains which property is where, and helps you land on the right booking for your itinerary rather than the first result you click.

Quick Answer: The best-known Pine Park property is Pine Park Hotel and Resorts in Shogran, Mansehra District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — a large, long-established resort spanning over two acres with rates from Rs. 20,500 to Rs. 28,500 per night. Separate listings such as Pine Park Glade Resort also operate in the area. Always verify the exact property name, address and contact number before paying an advance.

The Flagship: Pine Park Hotel and Resorts, Shogran

This is the property most people mean. It sits on the Shogran plateau at roughly 2,362 metres, occupies more than two acres of lawn, cottage blocks and standing pine, and is among the longest-established hotels in the valley. Arriving up the jeep track from Kiwai, it is the first major hotel on your left.

Full detail, live availability and the booking form are on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page.

Other Pine Park Listings in the Area

Pine Park Glade Resort Shogran appears as a separate listing — a smaller mountain property in the same area, described with continental breakfast, free Wi-Fi, free parking, a firepit and garden seating. It differs meaningfully from the flagship resort, most obviously in that breakfast is included where the larger property bills meals separately. We cover it in more depth in our Pine Park Glade Resort and Siri Paye base guide.

Because several properties share the Pine Park name in the Kaghan region, the practical rule is simple: match the address, not just the name. A booking confirmation should carry the full property name, the locality and a working contact number before any money changes hands.

Shogran or Naran: Which Base Do You Actually Want?

This is the question behind most “Pine Park Hotel Naran” searches. The two towns serve different trips.

If Siri Paye Meadows is your priority, stay in Shogran. If Lake Saif-ul-Malook is the goal, stay further up. Many travellers do both across a three or four night trip, moving up the valley rather than day-tripping in both directions.

Properties Along the Kaghan Valley

If you are building a multi-stop itinerary rather than a single base, these are the useful waypoints:

  • Parbat View Hotel and River Restaurant, Paras — lower in the valley, riverside, a natural break on the drive up from Balakot.
  • Pine Park Hotel and Resorts, Shogran — the plateau base for Siri Paye.
  • Sky View Hotel and Family Resort, Shogran — a lower-rate alternative on the same plateau.
  • Grand Vista Hotel, Shogran — another plateau option worth comparing.
  • Pine Wood Hotel and Family Cottage, Malakandi — mid-valley, useful heading toward Naran.
  • Fairyland Hotel and Restaurant, Malakandi Kaghan — another mid-valley option.

Current rates for all of them are on our Shogran and Kaghan hotels directory.

A Suggested Four-Night Kaghan Itinerary

  1. Day 1: Islamabad to Shogran via Mansehra, Balakot and Kiwai. Stop at Kawai Waterfall on the way. Check in and spend the evening on the lawn.
  2. Day 2: Early jeep to Siri Paye. Leave by 7:30 AM in peak season. Back by afternoon, bonfire in the evening.
  3. Day 3: Sharan Forest or Manna Meadows for a quieter contrast to the crowds at Siri Paye.
  4. Day 4: Move up the valley through Malakandi toward Naran and Lake Saif-ul-Malook.
  5. Day 5: Return to Islamabad.

Ready-made versions of this route, with transport and hotels arranged, are on our Shogran and Kaghan tour packages page.

Verifying Any Pine Park Booking

Before transferring an advance to any property in Kaghan, confirm:

  1. The full, exact property name as it appears on the confirmation
  2. The locality — Shogran, Malakandi, Naran or elsewhere
  3. A working phone number you have actually called
  4. The room category and rate in writing
  5. The cancellation window — Pine Park allows free cancellation up to 48 hours before check-in

Distances and Drive Times Across Kaghan

The number that catches people out is the last leg from Kiwai. It is short in distance but slow in practice, and it is the reason a sedan will not do. Plan your arrival so you are not attempting it after dark.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a Pine Park Hotel in Naran?

The best-known Pine Park property is in Shogran. Listings under similar names appear across the Kaghan region, so verify the exact locality and address before booking.

What is the difference between Pine Park Hotel and Resorts and Pine Park Glade Resort?

Pine Park Hotel and Resorts is the large, long-established Shogran property with five room categories and over two acres of grounds. Pine Park Glade Resort is a separate, smaller listing in the area that includes continental breakfast.

Should I stay in Shogran or Naran?

Shogran for Siri Paye Meadows and a forested, quieter setting. Naran for Lake Saif-ul-Malook and access deeper into upper Kaghan.

How much is Pine Park Hotel per night?

From Rs. 20,500 for a Standard Room up to Rs. 28,500 for the VIP/Executive category, with every room sleeping up to four guests.

How do I avoid booking the wrong property?

Match the address and contact number, not just the name, and book through a verified listing with published rates and a stated cancellation policy.

Start With the Right Base

Get the location right and the rest of the trip follows. Compare live rates on the Pine Park Hotel and Resorts Shogran page, review every property on our Kaghan hotels directory, or read our guide to choosing the best hotel in Shogran.
